sentences.text: Enterococcus faecalis is described as a significant resident of the gastrointestinal tract of most animals, including humans.
A review describes it as generally non-pathogenic in healthy hosts, but adept at exploiting compromised host immune function, which can result in life-threatening opportunistic infections.
The same review reports that treatment of those infections is complicated by a high degree of intrinsic and acquired resistance to antimicrobial chemotherapy.
Another review describes this commensal of the human gastrointestinal tract as able to cause severe illness in people with compromised immune systems, and as associated with secondary apical disease.
A systematic review and meta-analysis reported that rates of infective endocarditis in Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection vary more than 20-fold across published cohorts.
